security.title: Improper Initialization
security.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.

evidence.explanation: In VectorStoreController.loadVetDataToVectorStoreOnStartup(), the return value of convertListToJsonResource(vets) at line 74 is passed directly to new JsonReader(vetsAsJson) at line 75 without a null check. The convertListToJsonResource() method (lines 94-110) explicitly returns null when a JsonProcessingException is caught (line 108). Passing null to the JsonReader constructor will cause a NullPointerException at runtime, leaving the vector store in an uninitialized state.

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: In VectorStoreController.loadVetDataToVectorStoreOnStartup() at line 86, a temporary file is created via Files.createTempFile("vectorstore", ".json", attr) and written to disk. The file is never deleted after use — no file.delete() or deleteOnExit() is called. Each application restart creates a new temp file that accumulates on the filesystem, leading to resource exhaustion over time.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: VisitsServiceClient is a Spring @Component singleton (line 30) with a mutable non-final instance field 'hostname' (line 34). The field has a package-private setter setHostname() (lines 54-56) that modifies the shared field without synchronization. In a multithreaded web environment, concurrent threads invoking getVisitsForPets() could read a stale or partially written 'hostname' value if setHostname() is called concurrently, leading to undefined behavior.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: In application.yml at line 25, the OpenAI API key property uses a hardcoded default value of 'demo': `api-key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:demo}`. When the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is not set, the application will use 'demo' as the API key for outbound communication to the OpenAI API, constituting a hard-coded credential fallback.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: In application.yml at line 25, the OpenAI API key is configured with a hard-coded default value: `api-key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:demo}`. The string 'demo' serves as a hard-coded fallback credential used for authenticating to the OpenAI API when the environment variable is absent. This hard-coded credential may be used unintentionally in environments where the variable is not set (e.g., developer machines or misconfigured deployments).
